text:
elaine: ran a focused nsys + perfetto pass on the model-serving pod that regressed yesterday. attaching quick summary.

elaine: TL;DR: when prefix-cache hit-rate falls below ~72% we start seeing kernel-selection thrash (switching between our fused attention kernel and fallback single-head kernel), plus batching heuristics create a lot of small batches that avoid the fast path. overall token p99 latency up ~2.3x vs baseline.

sam: :eyes: can you paste the nsys command you used?

elaine: sure
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o run_kv_hotpath ./bin/serve --model gptx-6b --workload replay.json
```
I also exported the timeline and looked at kernel occupancy and launch times in perfetto.

ravi: interesting, is the cache miss spike correlated with certain routes or sequence lengths?

elaine: yes — two patterns:
- a burst of long seq requests (~1024 tokens) from `embedder-route` which invalidates some prefix segments (we don't shard by user there)
- many short chat completions (<=40 tokens) that hit fallback batching path because our dynamic batcher misclassifies them as tail requests

marco: do you have the KV stats dump?

elaine: pasted below (cut for brevity)
```
$ python tools/kv_stats.py --pod serving-3 --range 2026-02-01T10:00:00/2026-02-01T10:05:00
prefix_cache.requests: 15321
prefix_cache.hits: 11012
prefix_cache.misses: 4309
prefix_cache.evictions: 912
kv_cache.kv_requests: 15400
kv_cache.kv_hits: 10850
kv_cache.kv_misses: 4550
avg_prefix_reuse_depth: 0.38
```
hit-rate = 11012 / 15321 = 71.9% (yep)

jen: perf-bot posted an automated summary earlier: perf-bot: "warmup window=120s, observed 3x spike in misses at 10:02:14, coincident with a deploy of batching heuristic change"

perf-bot: deploy detected: commit 8f3a1e9 - tweak-batching: changed tail_batch_threshold from 8 -> 4

sam: that change would make small groups be routed to tail path more often (smaller threshold -> more tail batches). could explain small-batch amplification.

ravi: kernel-selection thrash — any kernel durations? can you paste the kernel timeline snippet?

elaine: from perfetto: timeline of attention kernels (time in ms)
```
0.0  - fused_attn      (cudaStream 2)  0.45 ms
0.5  - single_head_attn (cudaStream 2) 0.87 ms
1.4  - fused_attn      (cudaStream 2) 0.48 ms
2.0  - single_head_attn (cudaStream 2) 0.92 ms
2.9  - fused_attn      (cudaStream 2) 0.46 ms
```
pattern: back-and-forth every request — overhead from kernel selection + extra kernel launches ~0.3-0.5ms per token.

marco: do we have NVTX markers around the kernel selection code path? maybe selection runs on CPU and blocks stream synchronization.

elaine: yes we do. here's the nvprof-ish stack sample around the point of thrash:
```
# CPU timeline
select_kernel_variant() -> check_cache_meta() -> maybe_sync_and_warm_kv()
```
there's a sync in warm_kv to ensure loads, that causes stream stalls when a later request expects the fused kernel but the fallback was launched earlier.

jen: any quick mitigation we can flip? sticky kernel choice per shard? warmup prefetch?

sam: immediate: revert the tail_batch_threshold commit or set it back to 8. medium-term: prefer sticky kernel variant for N requests (cache temperature hysteresis) and decouple kernel selection from per-request latency-critical path (async prefetch of kernel artifacts).

ravi: we should also bias batching to prefer grouping small short requests together to hit the same prefix segments (increase reuse). maybe a short coalescing window for chat routes.

elaine: I ran a cheap experiment: reverted threshold locally and re-ran same nsys trace. hit-rate jumped to 85.6% and p99 latency dropped back to baseline.

elaine: experiment logs
```
before: hit_rate=71.9% p99=235ms
after (revert): hit_rate=85.6% p99=98ms
```

marco: sounds like a rollback for the live deploy until we implement sticky kernel/prefetch.

perf-bot: creating incident/ops ticket: #INC-2026-0421 - kv-prefix-cache regression after batching tweak (assigned: eng-runtime)

jen: i'll own the rollback unless someone else is on call.

sam: i'll open a follow-up PR for hysteresis and a perf test that exercises prefix cache miss bursts. add an nsys fixture to CI that fails if kernel-selection frequency > 20% over baseline.

elaine: added a short checklist for the rollback and follow-ups in the ticket. also attaching the raw nsys export and perfetto slice markers in the ticket for deeper analysis. :white_check_mark:

ravi: thanks, good catch. let's make sure we add unit/regression test that simulates interleaved long/short seq patterns.

jen: noted. rolling.

end of thread
